svg.title: TOPAK G1 — The trusted base: a component enters only if its failure can only subtract, or its identity is issued
svg.desc: ADR-0045 (Accepted (genesis) 2026.10.01, Batch 22, confirmation required C2 and C4) declares the trusted base row by row: a fixed schema, three classes and a refusal, thirty-one archetype rows in five groups (Annex A), and the reference's own declaration (Annex B), with the two rows that changed class after ratification and the one added since: T-0045-31, the TLA+ Proof System (B25, ADR-0046 §3). Tables below are drawn in full from the record; where the code has moved past Annex B (G9 §2.6, pending ADR-0033 A7 and ADR-0034 A2), the row's note says so.
svg.text: TOPAK · G1

text.tspan: The trusted base: a component enters only if its failure can only subtract, or its identity is issued

svg.text: ADR-0045 (Accepted (genesis) 2026.10.01, Batch 22, confirmation required C2 and C4) declares the trusted base row by row: a fixed schema, three classes and a refusal, thirty-one archetype rows in five groups (Annex A), and the reference's own declaration (Annex B), with the two rows that changed class after ratification and the one added since: T-0045-31, the TLA+ Proof System (B25, ADR-0046 §3). Tables below are drawn in full from the record; where the code has moved past
Annex B (G9 §2.6, pending ADR-0033 A7 and ADR-0034 A2), the row's note says so.

Annexes A and B are declaration records under ADR-0023, ratified with the record as record-level entries; no deployment declaration has been written (G9 §8). Drafted by the assistant at the custodian's request; every drafter's choice settled by ratification.

text.tspan: A component is a row only if its failure can only subtract, or its identity is issued

svg.text: "Adds authority" has an exact meaning (Context, from ADR-0015: authority changes are exactly promotion and anchor issuance, “changes to the rules in force”). It is one of three things, and nothing else counts:
(1) an admit the rules in force would refuse · (2) a promotion the tally would stall · (3) an issuance the rules floor would reject.
Break-glass is not an addition: it happens within the rules in force.
Subtractions (ADR-0031 §5): a denial, a lapsed lease, an ended round, a revocation, an epoch fence, a stalled promotion, lost evidence.

text.tspan: The classes as a decision (§2; the order of the questions is the diagram's)
A component the deployment relies on

svg.text: A program, a device, a person, a store or a value (§1, Component).
Does any theorem take a premise from it (its Trusted for sentence, a premise node, §3)?
Relied on in practice and trusted for nothing. The row exists so every theorem premised on it is
computed void, not silently assumed (§3 rule 1). Examples: T-0045-13 gate runner, 22 host at
rung 0, 23 native tool, 24 Run channel.
Can the worst it yields be one of the three additions, rather than a subtraction (Failure can
produce)?
Its failure can only subtract. No proof, no key, no quorum; may be commodity substrate;
declared per deployment, reopens nothing (ADR-0034 §5's delegation test, met four times in the
corpus). Examples: T-0045-4 clock, 5 Kafka, 6 bundle engines, 7 archive.

text.tspan: Is its identity fixed, and did it enter by its own record?

svg.text: Both: identity fixed by an anchor issuance (a key under ADR-0025 §1 (c) or (f), a roster
under (a) or (b)) or by a promotion (an artifact named by digest), so replacing it is an
authority change; and it entered by a record of its own (ADR-0023's non-increasing-TCB
rule).
Trusted although its failure can add. Its residual is what its holder can do while the identity
stands. Model: ADR-0034 §2's verifier (T-0045-17). Examples: T-0045-1 replicas, 2 signature, 3
Cedar engine, 28–30 what runs, 31 the prover.
Either it moves inside the verified object, where it is checked and not trusted, or the
design changes until its failure can only subtract. Applied in §6: trusted time refused; the
solver refused, and the proof checker that replaced it is a trust root (B24).
yes
yes
no
no
no: subtract only
yes, both

text.tspan: §1 · A row has a fixed schema

svg.text: What is trusted: a program, a device, a person, a store, a value
mechanism-boundary, substrate, toolchain or people (drafter's choice: ADR-0031 §6's three, plus ToO §13's people)
The premise the theorems take from it, in one sentence. This is the row's premise node in the theorem DAG (§3)
The axis and the rung range at which the premise is assumed. all for rung-0 rows
delegated, trust root or excluded (§2)
The worst thing the component's failure yields, named as a subtraction (ADR-0031 §5) or as one of the three additions above
For a trust root: the issuance (which ADR-0025 §1 item) or the promotion (which artifact, by digest) that names it. For a delegated row: the deployment declaration. For an excluded row: nothing
What remains when the component fails as named, stated on the face. Never empty; "none beyond the class" is a claim, stated as one
Custody is not a field: it is a pointer to a custody declaration (ADR-0025's annex or the deployment's), placed in Identity fixed by.

text.tspan: §6 · The rule applied to the 09.28 prioritization's eight candidates
Replicas: authentication and Byzantine replicas (G5, item 23)

svg.text: trust root (T-0045-1)
A Byzantine replica proposes admits no floor evaluated (ToO A9): an addition. Identity is the release's replica set, a promoted artifact. The residual is the forged admit;
mTLS is a delegated mitigation that prevents impersonation and not compromise. BFT is not required by this record
excluded (T-0045-23)
D-0034-3 already makes the principal Mediated. Nothing checks the tool; the row says so and every hermeticity premise is void for it
trust root (T-0045-16 to 18)
Their failure admits a rogue guest as Attested. Identity is P7's reference values in the promoted profile, and the verifier's issued key. The residual is on the face: side
channels and physical access, as ADR-0034 §6 states

text.tspan: Key custody and the anchor ceremony (G6)

svg.text: trust root (T-0045-8)
Key theft is a forged issuance. Identity is the anchor key set, item (c). The vault is delegated for availability and a trust root for secrecy; the row says which
A slow clock extends a break-glass approval, which preserves authority (ADR-0032 §2). No issuance fixes a clock's identity. The epoch-lapse stand-in is the subtract-only
answer, as the prioritization said; a time source enters only as a trust root with an attested identity, which no record has written
refused (finding 1); the checker that replaces it is a trust root
A false "implies" classes a relaxation as a tightening, and the relaxation then passes by promotion alone without the issuance ADR-0030 §5 requires. That is an addition,
and no key makes a solver honest. Either the routing check moves inside the verified object, or every floor change becomes two-key and the solver can only block.
ADR-0030 A1 (Batch 24) decided: a holds counts only with a proof a pinned checker accepted, so the solver is trusted for nothing and the checker is the row ⟨B24⟩
delegated (T-0045-7)
Its failure loses evidence, which subtracts legibility and never authority. The horizon and the audit read path are ADR-0028's rules, not the store's
not a row
Inside the verified object: the log is what the theorems are about. Service engineering, with no premise to declare

Also sorted: the gate runner (G8) is refused as delegated and admissible as a trust root once its evidence is signed under a key in issued rules (ADR-0025 §1 (f)); until then T-0045-13 is excluded and gate evidence is an operator's assertion (I18; G9 item 57). The rung-1 launcher is a trust root by
ADR-0036 §5's own list; the launcher in the node is built, pending ADR-0033 A7 (G9 item 35), and gives T-0045-19 and T-0045-20 a rung-1 instance (G9 §2.6).
An undeclared row is false: a deployment sits below every theorem whose premises include it.
Type changes are rows: an ADR-0023 §4a degeneracy changes a row's class or rung range; §6b's field is a list of row ids
(amendment owed, G9 item 64).
Membership per rung is the Rungs column; the per-round slice (ADR-0031 §6) is derived from the lease.
The binding table exists: spec/theorem-premise-binding.md (R6), 43 rows at G9, revised pending A7 and A2 (G9 §2.6). At
R6, three rows no theorem cited: T-0045-7, 21, 26. Since B25 the rows with a proof module (38 at G9) rest on T-0045-31 for the
invariant, in place of T-0045-29 (ADR-0046 §5).

text.tspan: §4 · Changing the table has a direction

svg.text: Removing a row, or trust root → delegated: a tightening; an ordinary promotion (archetype version at archetype level).
Adding a row, or delegated → trust root: a relaxation; its own record, and an issuance where it names a key (ADR-0034 added
A deployment instantiates rows; it does not add them. Trusting more is a §4a degeneracy with a D-row citing the T-row.
Annex A carries its archetype version; non-increasing TCB is checked row set against row set.

text.tspan: §5 · The verified object is the specification; what runs is a row

svg.text: Admit path, linked floor, Authentic, tally, rules floor, log: checked as specified (TLA+ with mutations at small constants, floor
gates, tests) and not trusted.
Since B25 (ADR-0046) the modules' invariants are proved with TLAPS, for every constant their assumptions admit: fifteen proof
modules at G9, 3,036 obligations (G9 §2.9). The prover is trust root T-0045-31, and TLC (T-0045-29) keeps the mutations and
witnesses.
What runs is not the specification (R1): no refinement from TLA+ to Rust, an asserted build. Hence trust roots T-0045-28 to 30
for every deployment; a proof is of the module, not of what runs.
A debt, owned by ADR-0033 (R2): the rows leave when a machine-checked chain is cited. Stage 1, trace validation, exists (R4),
and since G9 reads every traced state against the abstract confinement invariants (A7, A8 pending); stages 2–3 open (G9 item
Kind: declaration (ADR-0023 §6a). Parameter: the trusted-base declaration, published → absent.
Premises falsified: every row (§3 rule 1). Theorems voided: every theorem with a premise node; the bottom of every axis,
holding only the mechanism constants.
Type changes: none declared, which is the failure.
The reference's position before Annex B, and every deployment's before it declares.

text.tspan: Annex A · The archetype's trusted base: thirty-one rows in five groups (archetype version: the corpus at Batch 20, 2026.09.30; T-0045-31 added by dependent entry, B25)

delegated (failure only subtracts)
excluded (trusted for nothing; premised theorems void)

The admit path, the linked floor, Authentic, the tally, the rules floor and the log: the verified object (§5). Grant seats (ToO A4): the promotion quorum is the authority, not something trusted for it; their independence is ADR-0035's rule and their judgment is what ADR-0024 counts. Cell Observers and correlators: principals whose findings only subtract (ADR-0007); collusion is ADR-0039 §5's declared gap and lineage independence its cover, neither a trust row. The Listener and the Reader: stages that add nothing to the trusted base
(ADR-0037 §2, ADR-0043 §1). Trusted time: refused (§6).

With T-0045-13, 16 to 21, 22, 23 and 24 excluded or absent, every theorem premised on confinement, on gate evidence, on hermeticity and on channel fidelity is void at the reference. What remains are the mechanism constants and the theorems whose premises

are the all rows above: the lease, the fence, composition, the tally, the coupling, seats and Observers. Every one of those rests on T-0045-28 to 30 ⟨R1⟩: they hold of the modules, and of the running reference only on trust in the refinement nobody has made.

The invariants of the thirteen modules ADR-0046 proves rest on T-0045-31 in place of T-0045-29, and their mutations and witnesses on T-0045-29 still ⟨B25⟩. That is the honest inventory ADR-0033 §1 describes in prose, with its one unstated premise now stated.

svg.text: T-0045-27, the bundle signer: excluded → trust root, degenerate (B23, ADR-0033 A6): a dev bundle key generated by dev-init.sh, custody (1, 0). The inventory is unchanged: no theorem rests on T-0045-27 alone.

T-0045-14: refused solver → trust root proof checker (B24, ADR-0030 A1): ethos 8dc85c4 against cvc5's CPC signature, with floor/cvc5-checked binding a proof to its query. The solver is trusted for nothing; an unsat the checker does not accept reaches
cedar as unknown.
Still on the face (G9 item 69, open): 25 of the 10.01 run's holds are holds°, folded by cedar with no query, and rest on T-0045-3, not the checker.

T-0045-31, the TLA+ Proof System, added (B25, ADR-0046 §3): a toolchain trust root beside TLC's T-0045-29, since an unsound prover adds by accepting a false theorem. T-0045-29's residual gains a clause (small constants bound the mutations and
witnesses only), and the inventory sentence one (the thirteen proved invariants rest on T-0045-31 in place of T-0045-29). The inventory is otherwise unchanged; T-0045-28 is untouched.

Still on the face (G9 §8; items 73, 74, open): the prover's soundness is trusted as written; its 1.9 GB install is not tracked (since 2026.10.03 tools/TLAPS-PIN names its version, commit and short digest in the corpus, and the 1.6.0-pre release tag has since
been rebuilt, so a fresh install no longer yields the pinned binary), and the SMT backends' proofs are not rechecked by Isabelle (tlapm -C).

At G9 the record is unchanged (G9 §2.6): thirty-one rows, no class change. The code moved under pending addenda: T-0045-19 and 20 have a rung-1 instance, 16 and 17 are test keys in simulated runs only (A7; Annex B's dependent entries owed, item 81),
and T-0045-24's move to delegated is owed on A2's ratification (item 80).
